summary.text: Sydney Kamlager-Dove is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 37th District, first elected in 2022. Born in Chicago and a University of Southern California graduate, she worked in nonprofit arts and community organizations and as a staffer to a state senator before winning local office on the Los Angeles Community College Board in 2015, then the California Assembly (2018) and State Senate (2021). Her House website says she prioritizes land, economic justice, art and democracy.

paragraphs.text: Sydney Kamlager-Dove was born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1972, and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Southern California in 1994 and a master's degree in arts management and public policy from Carnegie Mellon University in 1996.
According to her official House biography, after graduating from USC she worked for Rebuild LA and the Los Angeles Festival, two Los Angeles nonprofits, on job creation and public arts programs.
Her career also included work as district director for then-State Senator Holly J. Mitchell and in the nonprofit, entertainment, education and government fields.

Kamlager-Dove was appointed to the Los Angeles County Commission on Children and Families in 2013 and elected to the Los Angeles Community College Board in 2015, later serving as president of the district's Board of Trustees.
She won the April 3, 2018 special election for California State Assembly District 54 outright and served in the Assembly until 2021, then served in the State Senate (District 30) from 2021 to 2022.
Kamlager-Dove was elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and took office in January 2023, succeeding Karen Bass in the 37th District.

According to her House website, she serves on the Foreign Affairs Committee, where she is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on South and Central Asia, and on the Judiciary Committee, and she is Whip of the Congressional Black Caucus, Co-Chair of the Congressional Brazil Caucus and Policy Co-Chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus.

The site says that through her Foreign Affairs work she helped secure the release of constituent Eyvin Hernandez, a Los Angeles County public defender detained in Venezuela for nearly two years, and that she passed the GRATEFUL Act on immigration of locally employed U.S. embassy staff.
Her official biography says she lives in the district with her husband, stepchildren and a rescue cat.
